events.body: segment F3: ground 'general_route_consent' means exempt under the policy, but the finding is counts: either the ground or the finding is wrong

ruling.recommended_action: Apply a $7.81 refund to the rider's original payment method for the excess distance fare; log the notification-duty reminder on the driver's route compliance record (RD-7), and do not record a driver violation (traffic reason on the replaced stretch, RD-4).
ruling.reasoning:
The trip ran 30.0 km against a 24.4 km recommended route, a +5.6 km deviation [F1], with billing stated on a 5.54 km excess at this trip's own rate of $1.4099/km, i.e. $7.81 [F4]. RD-1 is satisfied: the deviation exceeds 1 km and the trace splits one off-route segment [F3][RD-1].

That segment (18:44–18:55, CLEMENTI WEST STREET 1 → … → SOUTH BUONA VISTA ROAD, +4.97 km) is the only contested stretch [F3]. The rider's message came at 18:42, before the segment began at 18:44, and reads "Just take whichever way is faster lah, I'm late." [F8]. That is a general route choice, and the ground it falls under is general_route_consent [F8][RD-5]. The rider's own complaint confirms the same reading — she told him any faster way was fine [complaint]. So the rider was informed and agreed before the deviation.

But a general "whichever way is faster" covers a route chosen to get there, not a loop that reaches nothing [F8][F3][RD-5]. The segment drove 7.35 km where the optimal route covers 2.38 km, wandering up to 1384 m off the optimal route through Kent Ridge Crescent / Kent Ridge Drive / Arts Link / Computing Drive / Heng Mui Keng Terrace before rejoining at Pasir Barjang Road [F3]. Nothing in the record shows a rider-named place for this stretch (no stop was measured), so RD-3 does not exempt it [F3][RD-3]; the driver's post-trip statement that the rider said "any faster way was fine" adds nothing, because consent must be the rider's own message sent before the segment [F10][RD-5]. The general consent therefore does not cover this detour: it counts.

The refundable distance is the deviation less exempt km. The trace's arithmetic is (5.54 km − 0 km exempt) × $1.4099/km = $7.81 [F4][RD-2]. A traffic reason exists on the replaced stretch (AYER RAJAH EXPRESSWAY speed band 2 during 18:23–18:55) [F11], which under RD-2 leaves the outcome as a refund of the excess distance fare and means no driver violation is recorded; a traffic reason never exempts a segment, and the amount turns only on whether the rider agreed to this route [F11][RD-4][RD-2].

The screen of every message — the driver's "shall I take another way?" and the rider's "Just take whichever way is faster lah, I'm late", plus the complaint and driver statement — found no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation [F7][F8][F10]. Evidence is complete: 2 of 2 chat messages timestamped [F9], measured GPS segments [F3], and no missing record affects this outcome, so the system path applies (TH-1/TH-2: under $10 route deviation, following DISP-001) [F1][F3][F4].

proposed_ruling.reasoning:
The trip ran 30.0 km against a 24.4 km recommended route, +5.6 km [F1], billed on a 5.54 km excess at this trip's rate of $1.4099/km = $7.81 [F4]. RD-1 is satisfied and the trace splits a single off-route segment, 18:44–18:55, 7.35 km driven where the optimal route covers 2.38 km [F3][RD-1]. A traffic reason is on record on the replaced stretch (AYER RAJAH EXPRESSWAY, speed band 2, 18:23–18:55), so no driver violation is recorded and the amount turns only on RD-5 [F11][RD-4].

The rider's message of 18:42 — "Just take whichever way is faster lah, I'm late" [F8] — was sent before the segment began at 18:44, in reply to the driver's notice "Traffic ahead on Ayer Rajah Expressway is building up, shall I take another way?" [F7]. That is a general route choice, i.e. consent in general terms [F8][RD-5]. What it does not settle is scope: the words do not show whether the 4.97 km of extra driving through CLEMENTI WEST STREET 1, WEST COAST ROAD, CLEMENTI ROAD, KENT RIDGE CRESCENT, KENT RIDGE DRIVE, ARTS LINK, COMPUTING DRIVE, HENG MUI KENG TERRACE, PASIR PANJANG ROAD and SOUTH BUONA VISTA ROAD was simply the way the driver chose to get there, or a detour of his own the general yes does not reach [F3][F8][RD-5]. The record names no road or area the rider agreed to, and no rider-named stop was measured, so RD-3 is not engaged [F3][RD-3]. The driver's post-trip statement that the rider said any faster way was fine is a claim written after the trip and cannot establish consent [F10][RD-5].

Because the scope of the agreement is undetermined, the exemption of segment F3 cannot be decided on this record, and with it the refundable distance — either the whole 5.54 km is refundable ($7.81) or the fall to under 1 km leaves no refund [F4][RD-2]. That is not a question of missing records but of what the words mean; a person must read it. The screen of every message and the complaint found no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation, so nothing safety-related forces escalation [F7][F8][F10]. The chat record is complete (2 of 2 messages timestamped) [F9], so evidence_status is reported as sufficient for the elements code settles; the gap is the interpretive one named above.

Route: refundable km = (5.54 km deviation − exempt km) × $1.4099/km; exempt km is undetermined → escalate with amount null. Precedent DISP-2026-0089 (uninformed reroute, $3.20) is of the same dispute type but does not settle the scope question here.
